who: Ancient historian at Wayne State University; PhD University of Michigan, 1951.

evidence.says: Publisher biography identifies Finley Hooper as a Wayne State history professor from 1966 and gives his Michigan PhD in 1951.
A 1989 report identifies Wayne State historian Finley Hooper as the author of Roman Letters.
Authority names Finley Hooper and cites Roman letters (1990); it also records the fuller name Finley Allison Hooper.

notes: University, doctorate and authorship connect the supervisor to this authority.

who: UNLV historian of environmental and public history and the American West; PhD University of New Mexico.

evidence.says: UNLV identifies Andy Kirk as history professor and public history program director, with a PhD from the University of New Mexico.
Authority identifies Andy Kirk (Andrew Dewey) as a saxophonist and bandleader, citing Walkin' and swingin'.
Authority identifies A. E. (Abi E.) Kirk through the novel Loving in time and the Abi Kirk website.
Authority identifies the author of Data visualization (2012), a data visualization consultant with degrees from Lancaster and Leeds.

notes: All three supplied candidates identify other authors; none identifies the UNLV historian.

who: Robert Burr Litchfield, European historian at Brown, 1968–2003; history PhD Princeton, 1965.

evidence.says: Princeton memorial gives the 1965 history PhD, Brown appointment from 1968 to 2003, and authorship of Emergence of a Bureaucracy.
Authority for R. Burr Litchfield cites Emergence of a bureaucracy (1986) and explicitly identifies the Department of History at Brown University.

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the matching department; the memorial confirms the doctorate and supervision period.

who: Frederick D. Marquardt, Syracuse historian of German social, economic and labor history; PhD UC Berkeley.

evidence.says: Syracuse History Department newsletter, summer 2006, faculty directory p. 11, lists Frederick D. Marquardt, a Berkeley PhD specializing in German social, economic and labor history.
Authority identifies Frederic Sylvester Marquardt and cites The unchanging responsibility of the American newspaper in a changing society (1970).
Hamilton identifies Frederic Sylvester Marquardt as a newspaper journalist and editor, including the Philippines Free Press, Chicago Sun, Phoenix Gazette and Arizona Republic.

notes: The sole candidate is Frederic Sylvester Marquardt, the newspaper editor, rather than Frederick D. Marquardt of Syracuse.

who: James Mercer Merrill, Delaware historian of military and naval history; PhD UCLA, 1954.

evidence.says: AHA Perspectives, August 1995, memorial identifies James Mercer Merrill as a Delaware professor, appointed in 1966, with a UCLA PhD in 1954 and research in military and naval history.
Authority for James M. Merrill expands the name to James Mercer Merrill and cites The rebel shore (1957).

notes: The fuller name, institution, field and doctorate identify the naval historian among the supplied candidates.

who: Steven Merritt Miner, Ohio University historian of Russia, the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe; history PhD Indiana.

evidence.says: Ohio University identifies Steven M. Miner as history professor emeritus, specializing in Russian/Soviet and East European history, with an Indiana history PhD.
December 2001 university trustees minutes include Steven Merritt Miner as Professor of History and department chair.
Authority identifies Steven Merritt Miner, associates him with Indiana University, and cites Stalin's minimum aims.

notes: Ohio sources connect Steven M. and Steven Merritt Miner; the doctorate and field agree with the authority and AHA record.

who: Otis C. Mitchell, University of Cincinnati historian specializing in modern German history.

evidence.says: Authority for Otis C. Mitchell explicitly identifies the History Department at the University of Cincinnati and cites Hitler's Nazi state and a study of the Nazi SA.
September 1985 newsletter identifies Otis C. Mitchell as head of Cincinnati's History Department.
Autumn 1999 newsletter identifies Cincinnati historian Otis Mitchell as a specialist in modern German history.

notes: The authority explicitly supplies the matching department, and the society sources confirm the name and field.

who: Sasha Mullally, University of New Brunswick historian of medicine and health; PhD Toronto, 2005.

evidence.says: UNB identifies Sasha Mullally as history professor and graduate supervisor, with a Toronto PhD and a specialty in Canadian and American medical and health history.
Authority identifies Sasha Mullally through Unpacking the black bag (2005).

Scholarly society dissertation bibliography lists Sasha Mullally's Unpacking the Black Bag: Rural Medicine in the Maritime Provinces and Northern New England States, 1900–1950 as a Toronto PhD dissertation, 2005.
UNB's 2022–2023 history graduate handbook lists Sasha Mullally with specialties in modern Canada and the social history of medicine and health.

notes: The authority work is the matching Toronto dissertation; the UNB profile and contemporary handbook confirm the department and field.
